messages:
Maria Chen: FYI — last Sat 03:14 UTC we saw an odd shape: requests -32% vs baseline but aggregate tokens/hr +48% in us-west-2. GPU-hours up ~12% even though QPS dropped. Suspect long-tail prompts from partner A (new "full transcript" option for file summarization).

Ajay Patel: do we have per-customer token distribution for that window? any model swaps/canaries that could explain it?

Maria Chen: quick monitoring slice below:
```
window: 2026-03-14T03:00-04:00Z
requests: 12,000 (-32%)
tokens: 8,600,000 (+46%)
avg tokens/request: 717 (+115%)
p95 tokens/request: 6,400 (+320%)
p99 tokens/request: 24,000
avg GPU latency: 220ms (+60%)
GPU-hours (us-west-2): 83 (+12%)
prefix-cache miss rate: 18% -> 64%
```

Fernando Ramos: that avg tokens jump is huge — batching semantics will blow up. any runtime batching/window changes? min_batch_size?

Maria Chen: none on our side. partner A confirmed a client-side change: they started sending full transcript context instead of clipped summaries. Many requests now hit >4k sequence length; runtime still allocates KV for worst-case sequence which kills packing.

Lee Ng: request-level seq histogram changed: >4k went from 0.8% -> 8.9%. That explains the weird token/gpu-hours delta.

Zoe Park: partner eng acknowledged the rollback option. They said the feature was enabled for a small cohort at 02:50 UTC.

Sam Ortiz: short term ops plan: 1) apply per-customer token cap at edge (rate-limit tokens/request) 2) enforce max_seq=4096 for that partner to avoid huge KV allocations 3) route their heavy traffic to preemptible memory-optimized pool to absorb churn. Medium term: add dynamic batch-sizing to runtime to avoid huge kv allocations from single requests. Long term: surface per-customer token anomalies in billing.

Maria Chen: I applied a temporary routing rule to divert partner_A to the low-priority large-memory pool and added a token cap. Monitoring now: tokens/hr trending down, GPU-hours flattening.

route-bot: route-change: rule partner_A_token_cap applied to us-west-2 priority=low change_id=r-78b9 by Maria Chen

Ajay Patel: can you run a quick sim? if 10% of customers adopt full-transcript, what's monthly GPU-hour delta so finance can model cost exposure? ETA 24h would be great.

Maria Chen: back-of-envelope: current baseline monthly GPU-hours (us-west) ~120k. If 10% adopt and avg tokens/request x3, delta ~= +9.6k GPU-hours/month in us-west (~+8% local), cost delta roughly ~$45k/mo (ballpark using current spot blends). I'll refine if Ajay's sim gives different numbers.

Lee Ng: let's add a guardrail in Redwood Console: warn when avg tokens/request > 2x baseline per-customer for a rolling 1h window. Also flag large-seq request rate >1% for immediate alert. ETA 48h.

Zoe Park: I'll coordinate partner comms. They agreed to toggle the feature for the cohort and will push an immediate revert if we show negative infra impact.

Fernando Ramos: action items:
1) Ajay — run 6h sim and sensitivity curves (ETA 24h)
2) Lee — console guardrail + alert rule (ETA 48h)
3) Sam — draft billing FAQ + ops note for partner surcharge options (ETA EOD)
4) Maria — monitor route change and revert when partner toggles back (watch)

Sam Ortiz: drafting FAQ now, will cc legal for wording on retro billing.

Maria Chen: thanks all. I adjusted alert thresholds temporarily and will post a short incident note if this pattern reappears.

Ajay Patel: noted — I'll start the sim and drop results in this thread.

Zoe Park: :thumbsup: partner acknowledged and marked the rollout paused.

Maria Chen: closing loop for now — keep an eye on prefix-cache miss % and p99 tokens/request. If anyone sees another spike, ping infra-oncall and tag me.
